commitResults.messageBody:
Member collections can add and remove records but cannot replace details
while retaining the identity referenced by loans.

Add member replacement through the collection, root and model APIs.
Reject identity changes and resolve targets by normalized NUS ID so
edits preserve references and collection position.

Update the existing model test stub for the new interface so
intermediate commits remain compilable.

Members need to update contact details without recreating records or
disrupting existing loans.

Add a transactional member edit command that preserves omitted fields
and rejects edits that make no change. Open the updated member details
after execution.

Use the existing save-before-publish boundary so failed saves leave live
records unchanged.

commitResults.messageTitle: Route and validate member edit requests
commitResults.messageBody:
The member command family has no route for updating an existing member.

Route member edit to a dedicated parser that requires an exact NUS ID
and at least one editable field. Reuse member-add validation and
normalization for supplied names, phones and emails.

Reject blank, repeated and unknown fields with command usage guidance.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document member editing and its model contract
commitResults.messageBody:
The user guide describes member details as uneditable and the command
reference does not explain identity-preserving updates.

Document the edit syntax, unchanged-field behavior, validation and save-
failure guarantees. Describe directory refresh and the replacement API
for feature integration.

Keep soft-delete, restoration and archival deferred to later work.

Member editing needs regression coverage for stable identities,
unchanged fields, existing loans and rejected requests.

Add command, parser and collection tests plus real JSON and JavaFX
regressions. Exercise failed atomic saves and verify that edited
details, directory sorting and selection survive reload.

Verify 751 tests pass with production and test Checkstyle checks. The
new command and parser have full line and branch coverage.

Member deletion removes records and their closed loan history, making
accidental deletion permanent.

Add immutable deletion state and model operations that retain identity,
contact details and closed loans. Restore retained records without a
clock or recovery deadline.

Keep deleted identities reserved and reject open loans to deleted
members. Extend the existing model test stub for the restoration API.

Saved member records have no lifecycle state, so a restart cannot
preserve a recoverable deletion.

Persist the deleted boolean while treating absent legacy fields as
active. Reject explicit null and non-boolean values instead of silently
accepting invalid lifecycle state.

Keep closed-loan references valid and reject an entire load when an open
loan references a deleted member.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add member restore and lifecycle commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The member command family has no recovery operation and assumes every
stored member is active.

Add member restore using the existing transactional save boundary.
Reject repeated deletion and active-member restoration without saving,
and explain how to recover a deleted identity.

Block lending to deleted members and report deleted state in list and
view feedback while retaining records for selection and history.

commitResults.messageTitle: Style deleted members in the directory
commitResults.messageBody:
Retained deleted members need to remain selectable while being visually
distinct from active members.

Grey deleted cards and render names in italics with a strikethrough and
a separate deleted suffix. Preserve readable selected text and keyboard
focus indicators.

Reuse the same name treatment in details, show restoration guidance and
distinguish active, deleted and displayed directory counts.

The user guide and ownership contracts describe member deletion as
permanent and discard its closed loans.

Document retained records, unlimited restoration, reserved identities,
loan eligibility and the deleted-card presentation. Explain legacy JSON
defaults and invalid lifecycle flags.

Record the integration boundaries for the separate edit, transfer and
history workstreams. Keep equipment deletion and archival outside this
change.

Existing deletion tests expect member records and closed history to
disappear, so they do not verify recoverable lifecycle behavior.

Add model, command, parser, JSON and JavaFX regressions for retained
identity, reserved IDs, unlimited restoration and loan eligibility.
Verify partial-write and atomic-move failures preserve live state and
saved bytes.

Update prior expectations and check grey cards, name styling, selection,
counts, wrapping and fresh reloads. Run the full suite, Checkstyle and
coverage tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge upstream member editing into soft-delete
commitResults.messageBody:
Upstream master includes member editing, which conflicts with retained
member deletion and can silently restore deleted records during edits.

Resolve the command routing, model, UI tests and documentation conflicts
while preserving both features. Reject edits to deleted members with
restore guidance and prevent replacements from changing lifecycle state.

Editing a deleted member must preserve deletion state and saved data,

Cover deletion, rejected changed and unchanged edits, restoration and

Verify model replacements cannot bypass lifecycle restrictions or alter
loan history.

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement directory search and inventory planning
commitResults.messageBody:
Member and equipment directories offer fixed ordering and no partial
search. Inventory planning needs filters and grouped availability to
help users locate records and assess stock without changing data.

Add partial searches, filters, selectable sorting and duplicate
warnings. Derive inventory counts by category and equipment type, and
carry query criteria through typed display requests so the UI shows
matching rows.

Keep search commands read-only to avoid unnecessary persistence. Add
parser, query and real-shell tests, user documentation and screenshots.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep inventory category and type groups distinct
commitResults.messageBody:
Inventory grouping joins category and type with a display separator.
Values containing that separator can produce the same key for distinct
groups, combining their availability counts incorrectly.

Use separate category and type fields as the grouping key and sort by
both fields. Quote display labels so their boundaries stay clear even
when a value contains a separator or quotation mark.

Add collision regressions and update the documentation and screenshots
to verify that distinct groups retain their own counts and labels.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge master and retain edit and search routes
commitResults.messageBody:
Team master adds member editing while this branch adds search.
The two changes conflict in the member parser's diagnostic text.

Merge the team baseline and retain both routes and their names in
the error message. Preserve the incoming edit tests and persistence
changes so the combined branch supports both features.

Validate the integrated edit/search parsers and both Checkstyle
checks before recording the merge.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve search criteria after directory deletions
commitResults.messageBody:
Deleting a member or equipment item sends a plain directory request.
Treating every such request as a reset discards the active filters
and sort, and can show unrelated rows after the last match is gone.

Preserve the active query on plain directory navigation. Make list
commands explicitly request an unfiltered default-order query so
users can still reset the directory deliberately.

Add real-shell regressions for both deletions, remaining/zero-match
results, selection recovery, single saves and explicit list resets.
Update typed-request expectations and verify that merged member edit
and search routes remain available together.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge member lifecycle with search and planning
commitResults.messageBody:
Team master retains deleted members and adds restoration. Search
also changes member routing, directory counts and list requests,
causing conflicts across those shared contracts.

Merge master while preserving search, edit and restore routes.
Keep list/reset showing retained rows and count only active members
as active. Add explicit lifecycle filters to search so deleted
records remain discoverable without inflating active results.

Exclude deleted records from similarity warnings and preserve the
existing identity-reuse rejection. Verify delete/search/restore,
query retention, grey cards, accurate counts and JSON reloads.
